articles.title: Do we classify and treat consistently? A retrospective, two-centre observer agreement study of Neer classification and treatment selection for proximal humerus fractures.
articles.authors: Palafox Carral I, Goinikman Braverman J, Colin Lara X, Rivero Celaya BO
articles.outcomes: Interobserver and intraobserver agreement for Neer classification; association between Neer category and treatment recommendation
articles.take_home: The Neer classification system for shoulder fractures has only moderate reliability when different doctors classify the same fractures. The classification system does influence treatment decisions, with more complex fractures and older patients more likely to receive shoulder replacement rather than surgical repair.

articles.title: Reverse shoulder arthroplasty after failed tendon transfer: A systematic review of clinical outcomes and complications from the FP-UCBM shoulder study group.
articles.authors: De Rosa A, Cardinale ME, Paciotti M, Franceschetti E, Ciuffreda M, Di Fabio S, et al.
articles.population: Patients who had reverse shoulder arthroplasty after a failed or symptomatic tendon transfer for massive irreparable rotator cuff tears
articles.sample_size: 77 tendon transfers (70 shoulders with transfer-specific outcome data) across 5 studies; mean age 63 years
articles.outcomes: Pain reduction (VAS 6.2-8.3 to 0.3-2.2), forward elevation gain (+26 to +74 degrees), Constant score gain (14-45 points), ASES score gain (16.5-23 points), external rotation (small gains), complications in 25.7% (mostly instability), reoperations/revisions up to 37%
articles.take_home: Reverse shoulder surgery after failed tendon transfer reliably reduces pain and restores the ability to lift the arm forwards, but patients experience more complications and need more repeat surgery than those having primary reverse shoulder surgery, and rotational movement of the shoulder is rarely restored.

articles.title: Does cemented versus uncemented humeral stem fixation influence outcomes in primary reverse shoulder arthroplasty? An updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Sain B, Pal A, Suryawanshi S, Mishra P, Joseph R, Qadir W, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary reverse shoulder arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported outcomes, range of motion, revision rates, complications, radiographic findings, and tuberosity healing
articles.take_home: Cemented and uncemented humeral stems produce similarly good clinical results and revision rates in reverse shoulder arthroplasty. Although cemented stems showed more X-ray changes like loosening and radiolucency, these differences did not lead to worse function or higher revision rates in the follow-up period available.

articles.title: Translation and cultural adaptation of the Oxford Shoulder Score to Swedish and validation of a new 7-day recall version in patients with a proximal humerus fracture.
articles.authors: Lundin PC, Sundh TFD, Adolfsson LE, Bjornsson Hallgren HC
articles.population: Patients with non-operatively treated proximal humerus fracture
articles.outcomes: Convergent validity with QuickDASH, internal consistency, responsiveness to change, and intra-rater reliability of Swedish Oxford Shoulder Score
articles.take_home: The Swedish version of the Oxford Shoulder Score works well for measuring shoulder pain and function in patients with broken upper arm bones. A new 7-day recall version performs equally well and may be better for tracking early recovery after fractures.

articles.title: Careful with that motion: A prospective cohort study evaluating the relationship of passive shoulder motion on repair integrity in 136 consecutive arthroscopic rotator cuff repairs.
articles.authors: Looi DR, Bilog AMR, Lam PH, Khalaf M, Murrell GA
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary arthroscopic supraspinatus repair
articles.outcomes: Repair integrity assessed by ultrasound at 6 months; retear rate in relation to passive range of motion and patient-reported stiffness at 6, 12 and 24 weeks
articles.take_home: Patients who had greater passive shoulder motion in the first 6 to 12 weeks after rotator cuff repair were more likely to experience retear, with risk increasing gradually across the full range of motion. Those reporting no stiffness at 6 weeks had a much higher retear rate (26%) compared to those with some stiffness (4%).

articles.title: Distal Humerus Nonunion Following Failed Internal Fixation: How do the Outcomes of Internal Fixation and Total Elbow Arthroplasty Compare?
articles.authors: Nieboer M, Yu K, Tangtiphaiboontana J, Barlow J, Morrey M, Sanchez-Sotelo J, et al.
articles.population: Patients with distal humerus nonunion following failed internal fixation
articles.sample_size: 70 elbows (25 treated with S.O.S. technique, 45 treated with total elbow arthroplasty)
articles.outcomes: Union rates, complications, reoperations, range of motion (flexion-extension and pronation-supination arcs), and Mayo Elbow Performance Scores
articles.take_home: Both the S.O.S. technique and total elbow arthroplasty produced similar overall results for distal humerus nonunions, but the choice of treatment should depend on the type of nonunion: total elbow arthroplasty worked better for nonunions within the joint, whilst the S.O.S. technique worked better for nonunions outside the joint.

articles.title: No Difference in Revision Risk for Uncemented Humeral Stems Compared to Cemented Humeral Stems in Reverse Total Shoulder Arthroplasty for Proximal Humerus Fracture: A Registry-Based Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Chauhan A, Chang RN, Prentice HA, Cruz JR, McQueen PD, Paxton EW, et al.
articles.population: Adult patients undergoing reverse total shoulder arthroplasty for proximal humerus fracture
articles.outcomes: All-cause revision at 5-year follow-up; revision for dislocation and infection
articles.take_home: Uncemented and cemented humeral stems had similar revision rates (3.9% versus 3.2%) in reverse total shoulder arthroplasty for proximal humerus fracture, with no meaningful difference in risk of revision, dislocation or infection between the two fixation methods.

articles.title: 18-years Follow-up after Mosaicplasty in Adolescent Athletes with Osteochondritis Dissecans of the Elbow.
articles.authors: Toftdahl L, Ovesen J, Thillemann TM
articles.population: Adolescent athletes with unstable osteochondritis dissecans of the elbow capitellum treated with autologous osteochondral mosaicplasty
articles.outcomes: Mayo Elbow Performance Score, Oxford Elbow Score, Quick-DASH, range of motion, radiographic osteoarthritis grading, functional status
articles.take_home: After 18 years, most patients had good elbow function with minimal symptoms, though two patients showed early signs of osteoarthritis without pain. The results suggest mosaicplasty is a reasonable surgical option for this condition, but long-term osteoarthritis risk remains a concern.

articles.title: Newer Generation DePuy INHANCE Modular Anatomic Convertible Polyethylene Glenoid and Platform Baseplate have Improved Resistance to Micromotion and Dissociation at the Polyethylene-Metal Junction.
articles.authors: Kane LT, Myers C, Smith M, Cuff D, Jawa A, Wiater JM, et al.
articles.population: Shoulder arthroplasty implant components (not human subjects)
articles.outcomes: Resistance to micromotion, tensile displacement, and polyethylene dissociation under repetitive and shear loading
articles.take_home: A newer DePuy INHANCE shoulder implant design showed less movement and better resistance to coming apart compared to older all-plastic designs and competitor modular systems when tested under worst-case mechanical loading. These laboratory findings suggest the design may be more durable, though real patient outcomes still need to be confirmed.

articles.title: Glenohumeral radial mismatch and revision for aseptic loosening after anatomic total shoulder arthroplasty: a Dutch Arthroplasty Register study.
articles.authors: Boulidam D, Macken AA, Buijze GA, Spekenbrink-Spooren A, Sierevelt IS, Eygendaal D, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary anatomic total shoulder arthroplasty with Walch A glenoids and fully cemented all-polyethylene glenoid components
articles.outcomes: Revision for aseptic glenoid loosening (primary), revision for instability and revision for any cause (secondary)
articles.take_home: The study found that the difference in fit between the shoulder ball and socket (radial mismatch) did not affect how long the glenoid component lasted or the risk of it loosening. There was a suggestion that larger mismatches might increase instability risk, but this was based on very few cases and needs further study.

articles.title: Functional outcomes over 24 months after arthroscopic repair of isolated subscapularis tendon tears in a multicentre study.
articles.authors: Audige L, Croci E, Trong MLD, Flury M, Jost B, Cunningham G, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary arthroscopic repair for isolated subscapularis tendon tears
articles.outcomes: Range of motion, pain levels, abduction strength, Constant Score, Oxford Shoulder Score, Subjective Shoulder Value, EQ-5D-5L, adverse events, and patient satisfaction at 24 months
articles.take_home: Arthroscopic surgery for isolated subscapularis tears improved pain, strength and function over 24 months, though patients with partial tears had more residual pain and lower satisfaction rates than those with full-thickness tears.

articles.title: Fear-avoidance beliefs influence preoperative but not postoperative outcomes after arthroscopic rotator cuff repair.
articles.authors: Yamakado K, Nagamoto H, Katsutani H, Suzuki K, Satake H, Inoue J, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing arthroscopic rotator cuff repair
articles.outcomes: Preoperative and 12-month postoperative shoulder function (ASES, SANE, VAS scores) and fear-avoidance beliefs (FABQ-PA, FABQ-W scores)
articles.take_home: Fear-avoidance beliefs weakly influenced how patients perceived their shoulder function before surgery, but did not predict how well they recovered after arthroscopic rotator cuff repair at 12 months. This suggests that patients' anxiety about movement before surgery does not determine their actual recovery.

articles.title: Relative Real-time Arthroscopic Evaluation of Glenohumeral Structural Failure during Manipulation under Anesthesia for Primary Frozen Shoulder.
articles.authors: Abdel-Mordy Kandeel A, Lasheen MM, Ali Elsayed AF, Morsi E
articles.study_type: Prospective case series with real-time arthroscopic evaluation
articles.outcomes: Post-manipulation glenohumeral structural disruptions on second-look arthroscopy; passive range of motion immediately and at 6 months; pain (VAS) and shoulder function (ASES) scores at 6 months
articles.take_home: Manipulation under anaesthesia for frozen shoulder improved movement without causing major capsular tears in any patient, though minor injuries to shoulder structures occurred in some cases. Patients had significant improvements in movement and function up to 6 months after the procedure.

articles.title: Long-term clinical outcomes of distal biceps tendon reconstruction using fascia lata allograft.
articles.authors: Fawzy H, Hilgersom NFJ, Nijs A, Oost IK, Eygendaal D, The B
articles.population: Adult patients with distal biceps tendon rupture treated with fascia lata allograft reconstruction
articles.outcomes: Functional outcomes (QuickDASH score, Oxford Elbow Score), complications, patient satisfaction, return to work and sports
articles.take_home: Fascia lata allograft reconstruction for distal biceps tendon rupture produces good long-term function with high satisfaction, though complications occurred in 44% of patients, mostly minor issues like temporary nerve irritation that usually resolved.

articles.title: Cost-Effectiveness of Open Reduction Internal Fixation Versus Radial Head Arthroplasty for Mason III/IV Radial Head Fractures: A Decision Analytic Markov Model.
articles.authors: Kumar R, Salman SG, Bouras A, Rice SW, Shen O, Cheng C, et al.
articles.study_type: Cost-effectiveness analysis using Markov decision model
articles.population: Patients with Mason type III and IV comminuted radial head fractures
articles.outcomes: Cost per quality-adjusted life year (QALY), incremental cost-effectiveness ratio, net monetary benefit over 10 years
articles.take_home: Radial head replacement appeared more cost-effective than surgery to repair the broken bone, gaining more quality of life for a reasonable extra cost of approximately £9,600 per year of good health, though this depended on assumptions about how well each treatment actually works in practice.

articles.title: Stemless Anatomic Total Shoulder Arthroplasty is Associated with Less Opioid Use at Initial Follow-up.
articles.authors: Krumm ZR, Denard PJ, Brockmeier SF, Petre D, Kissenberth M, Shah A, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing anatomic total shoulder arthroplasty (short-stem or stemless)
articles.outcomes: Postoperative pain at 10-14 days (Visual Analog Scale), opioid use and refill requirements
articles.take_home: Patients having stemless shoulder replacements used less opioid pain medication at their two-week follow-up visit compared with those having short-stem replacements, although pain scores were similar between the two groups.

articles.title: Diagnosis and Management of Quadrilateral Space Syndrome Using Arthroscopic, Extra-Capsular Axillary Nerve Release.
articles.authors: Whitelaw K, Vasquez D, Wiley N, Macksood J, Elhassan B, Lohre R
articles.population: Patients diagnosed with quadrilateral space syndrome
articles.sample_size: 60 patients (40 underwent arthroscopic release, 20 received injection alone)
articles.outcomes: Pain scores (VAS), PROMIS Short Form 7a, quick disabilities arm shoulder hand (qDASH) score, external rotation range of motion, and complication rates
articles.take_home: Arthroscopic surgery to release the axillary nerve in the quadrilateral space significantly reduced pain and improved shoulder function in most patients, with low complication rates over an average follow-up of 29.5 months. Pain relief from surgery was comparable to that achieved with diagnostic injections alone.

articles.title: Upper body posture affects three-dimensional scapula orientation: Clinically applicable models may quantify patient-specific scapula orientation in an upright standing patient.
articles.authors: Ritter D, Dampier K, Olmsted AD, Poltaretskyi S, Raiss P, Bachmaier S, et al.
articles.population: Database of 123 lateral photographs of patients
articles.outcomes: Ability to predict three-dimensional scapula orientation (internal rotation, anterior tilt, upward rotation) from upper body posture measurements taken from standing photographs
articles.take_home: Simple measurements from side-on photographs of a patient standing upright can predict how their shoulder blade is positioned in three dimensions. This could help surgeons plan shoulder replacement operations more accurately by understanding the patient's natural upright posture, rather than relying only on CT scans taken while lying down.

articles.title: The interaction of race and insurance type on length of stay and discharge disposition following reverse total shoulder arthroplasty: A statewide database study.
articles.authors: Morriss NJ, Jeong A, Shaikh HJ, Greif DN, Ramirez G, Thirukumaran C, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing reverse total shoulder arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Length of stay and discharge disposition (home versus other)
articles.take_home: Black patients with commercial insurance had longer hospital stays and were less likely to go home after reverse shoulder surgery compared to White patients with similar insurance, suggesting healthcare disparities exist in how patients are managed after this operation.
